about: MUTATING — finish (or undo) a move-volume-replica-to-disk that stopped after its rebuild and before its delete: retire ONE named replica of ONE Longhorn volume whose node holds exactly one other replica of it on another disk (infra/forge/move-volume-replica.sh --finish <volume> <replica> <plan_sha256>; backlog 6d0b3c96), through the forge's ops_kubectl door. WHY: the signed move 02035ff0 (2026-11-17) left boss/pgdata-postgres-0 at 4 healthy replicas on 3 nodes, w-3 holding the old one on its default disk and the new one on u-postgres, because the rebuild of a ~95 GiB volume outlasted the move's 1200 s wait; no verb could take that state further, and a move killed outright (SIGKILL, OOM, host loss) or whose put-back was refused leaves the same shape with the move's diskSelector and replicaSoftAntiAffinity still set, undone only by hand kubectl (review 1c413d8d finding 3). AUTHORISED PER RUN BY David's passkey in design 17835005's shape: it declares requires_approval with the read-only plan-a-volume-replica-move-finish (this script's --plan-finish) as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders and changes nothing unless today's plan hashes to it. The count, the replicas and both fields are in the bytes, so a second run of an applied plan is refused: at most once. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S, NEVER A PARAM: every replica healthy and active, M on M-1 distinct nodes, the named one's node holding exactly one other on another disk, the declared count M or M-1, robustness healthy, the move's trim bounds, the anti-affinity enabled only as the move's held state, and the selector after admitting every remaining replica's disk — or nothing is done (exit 78). THE WRITE is the move's own steps 3 and 4: (1) ONE compare-and-set that tests spec.numberOfReplicas as declared and the two fields as read, lowers M -> M-1 (unless a stopped finish already did) and, only from the move's held state, puts spec.diskSelector [] and spec.replicaSoftAntiAffinity ignored — the patch is in the signed plan verbatim; (2) after 30 s of reads in which no replica was removed, a delete of the named replica by name — lower first, so Longhorn does not replace it; (3) a read-back for up to 180 s: the named replica gone, spec.numberOfReplicas M-1, M-1 healthy replicas on M-1 distinct nodes with the one that stays on its planned disk, both fields as the patch left them, robustness healthy; only then is the effect line printed, and otherwise the run exits 1 naming what it read. A disk short of the volume's next growth is named beside the effect, not judged: deleting a replica changes no remaining disk. No pod, engine or attachment is touched. A stop after the compare-and-set and before the delete leaves M replicas at count M-1, which a NEW plan of this verb signs and finishes. Timeout 600: the script's own waits (30 + 180 s) give its verdict before the runner's kill.
effect: ^finish-volume-replica-move: pvc-[0-9a-f-]{36} has [0-9]+ healthy replicas on [0-9]+ distinct nodes \([a-z0-9-]+(, [a-z0-9-]+)*\) — [0-9a-z-]+-r-[0-9a-f]{8} is gone, [0-9a-z-]+-r-[0-9a-f]{8} stays healthy on [a-z0-9-]+ disk (u-[a-z0-9-]+|default-disk-[0-9a-f]+) \(diskUUID [0-9a-f-]+\) — read back: spec\.numberOfReplicas=[0-9]+, spec\.diskSelector .+, spec\.replicaSoftAntiAffinity [a-z]+, robustness healthy
